newsitem.title: USA: Sacramento, Calif., proposes $70-mln loan for team.
newsitem.headline: Sacramento, Calif., proposes $70-mln loan for team.

text.p: Sacramento officials on Monday unveiled a detailed plan to provide the National Basketball Association's Kings with a $70 million loan to keep the team playing in the city.
The plan, which will be presented to the Sacramento City Council on Tuesday, calls for a 30-year loan for $70 million at the city's cost of borrowing.
The financing costs would not exceed $17.9 million, according to a summary of the proposal, released late on Monday in Sacramento.
The Sacramento Kings would pay the city the annual debt service each year from arena revenues and ticket surcharges.
The $87.9 million total cost of issuance would, however, be secured by the full faith and credit of the city.
City officials said Sacramento's general fund would be protected by $120 million in loan collateral, including a $20 million note secured on the Kings' franchise.

Under the terms of the proposed deal, all loan proceeds would be used by the team to retire existing debt. The Kings would also sign a 30-year lease. The team would have to pay off the entire debt if it were to leave Sacramento early.
City officials said they did not expect the financing to affeect the city's credit ratings.

Kings owner Jim Thomas had originally proposed a $235 million public-private partnership with the city of Sacramento to develop a sports and entertainment complex. The proposal included $90 million to retire his existing debts.
However, the $235 million proposal came under fire and was withdrawn by Thomas in late January.
